//: Story Phase 7, chapter 34: Which Away? A shorter return to the Sharkstorm survival from Phase 6 (the same deck layer: sharks overhead, telegraphed landings that only ever knock the captain flat). Make the loose rigging fast, reef the mainsail, keep Squawks close (inside the captain's coat), heave a shark over the side, and take the helm. The captain has never steered round a cyclone made of sharks; nobody has. 'AWAY.' 'Which away?' 'That is an excellent question.' Meanwhile the Grand Stenchmaster is furious. Not about the storm: about his television. Franklin has an audit hearing tonight.
p7c2.begin: The light goes out of the day as if somebody had shut a door on it. The column is right on top of the ship now, roaring, and sharks are coming out of it the way water comes out of a bucket.
captain[determined]: Make the rigging fast! Get the main in before it rips! Clear anything that lands! And somebody watch the sky!

p7c2.begin.tutorial: Hold her together: make the loose rigging fast (the port main shrouds; the starboard fore shrouds), reef the mainsail (the foot of the mainmast), and keep Squawks close (his basket). Watch the deck: a red ring and a growing shadow means a shark is coming down there. Step off it.
p7c2.begin.title: Which Away?

p7c2.line_a: The port main shrouds have worked loose and are whipping about like a dropped hose.
p7c2.line_b: The starboard fore shrouds, banging against the rail every time the ship rolls.
p7c2.reef: The mainsail is bellied out hard, yellow-stained, and humming. If it isn't reefed it'll tear, and then the mast might go with it.
hale[alarmed]: Haul it in, Captain! Before it takes us up into that thing like a kite!
Up it comes, reef by reef, until there's nothing left aloft for the wind to get a grip on.
p7c2.squawks: Squawks is pressed flat in the bottom of his basket, under every blanket he has, glaring at the sky.
captain[tender]: Come on. You're coming with me.
You unbutton your coat, scoop him up, blankets and all, and button him in against your chest, with just his head out at the top.
captain: Aye. Stay in there. Whatever happens.
p7c2.deck_shark: A whistle, falling. A shadow growing on the planks, forward of the main hatch.
THUMP. A big one. It lands across the deck forward of the main hatch and starts thrashing, and the crew scatter.

p7c2.deck_shark.tutorial: Shark on deck! Heave it over the side (forward of the main hatch).
p7c2.deck_shark.title: Which Away?

p7c2.heave: Gristle, Pete and Brask pile in beside you. A whole shark, wet, angry, and smelling faintly of the Grand Stenchmaster.
pete[alarmed]: This is the SECOND TIME THIS WEEK I've done this!
Over it goes. From inside your coat, a muffled voice says something unrepeatable.
The Revenge heels hard. Up on the quarterdeck, Nell is fighting the wheel.
p7c2.helm: You take the wheel from Nell. It kicks like a mule. The column is off the starboard bow, filling half the sky, and the sharks are coming out of it in sheets.
Thirty years at sea. Hurricanes. Waterspouts. Reefs in the dark. A frigate with forty guns. You have never once had to steer round a cyclone made of sharks.
Nobody has. There isn't a chart for it. There isn't a word for it, except the one Garrick gave it.

then: captain[tired]: Nell, I'm going to be honest with ye.

p7c2.helm: captain[tired]: That is an excellent question.
You put the helm over anyway, hard, so the column's on the quarter and not the bow. The Revenge comes round, groaning, and runs. Away. In general.
And then, from the middle of the deck, over the storm, over the sharks, over everything, a voice of pure fury.
nell[surprised]: Is he finally upset about the storm?

p7c2.helm.tutorial: Find out what the Grand Stenchmaster is shouting about (his chair, by the S.E.S.).
p7c2.helm.title: Which Away?

p7c2.garrick: The Grand Stenchmaster is on his feet beside his chair, red in the face, pointing a shaking glove at the broken S.E.S.
garrick[annoyed]: Look at it, Captain. LOOK at it.
captain: The storm?
garrick[annoyed]: The TELEVISION.
garrick[annoyed]: A shark came through that rail two nights ago and went straight through my set. Nobody has done anything about it. Nobody has even ASKED.
captain[angry]: We have been rained on by sharks!
garrick[annoyed]: And I have been rained on by sharks WITHOUT A TELEVISION.
Pete arrives, soaked, with a line over his shoulder and a bite out of his hat.
pete[annoyed]: WE ARE BEING RAINED ON BY SHARKS.
garrick[annoyed]: I KNOW.
pete[annoyed]: AND YOU'RE WORRIED ABOUT A FROG DOING TAXES?
garrick[offended]: Franklin has an audit hearing tonight.
bob[disgusted]: FRANKLIN IS NOT THE PRIORITY.
garrick[businesslike]: That is an irresponsible attitude toward financial compliance, Bob.
bob[surprised]: ...
garrick[worried]: It's the finale of the season, Captain. Seventeen seasons of build-up. If I miss it I'll have to wait for the repeat, and the repeats are out of order.
rook[surprised]: Repeats?
garrick: I had the last four episodes saved, of course. Recorded. For emergencies like this one. All gone.
crew: HOW?
garrick[smug]: Grand Stenchmaster technology.
Nobody asks a second time.
